translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing also asked that a capable registrar be sent out to receive and explain; the Liang emperor sent Palace Secretaries He Ji and Chief Clerk Guo Baoliang with Siyu to greet him at Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 景北面受敕，季曰：「今者之舉何名？

translations.literal: Jing faced north to receive the edict; Ji said, "What is the name of this present campaign?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing faced north to receive the edict; He Ji said, "What is the name of this present campaign?

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「欲為帝也！

translations.literal: " Jing said, "I wish to be emperor!
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing said, "I wish to be emperor!

sentences.zh: 」王偉進曰：「朱異等亂政，除奸臣耳。

translations.literal: " Wang Wei stepped forward and said, "Zhu Yi and the others disorder government—merely to remove wicked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Wei stepped forward and said, "Zhu Yi and the others disorder government—merely to remove wicked ministers.

sentences.zh: 」景既出惡言，遂留季，獨遣寶亮還宮。

translations.literal: " Jing having spoken evil words, he then detained Ji and sent only Baoliang back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Having spoken evil words, Hou Jing detained He Ji and sent only Guo Baoliang back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞景至，競入城，公私混亂，無復次第，羊侃區分防擬，皆以宗室間之。

translations.literal: When the people heard Jing had arrived, they rushed into the city; public and private affairs fell into chaos without order; Yang Kan organized defenses, placing members of the imperial clan between units.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard Hou Jing had arrived, they rushed into the city; public and private affairs fell into chaos; Yang Kan organized defenses, placing members of the imperial clan between units.

sentences.zh: 軍人爭入武庫，自取器甲，所司不能禁，侃命斬數人，方止。

translations.literal: Soldiers fought to enter the armory and take weapons and armor themselves; the officials could not stop them until Kan ordered several men beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers fought to enter the armory and take weapons and armor themselves; the officials could not stop them until Yang Kan ordered several men beheaded.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁興四十七年，境內無事，公卿在位及閭裡士大夫罕見兵甲，賊至猝迫，公私駭震。

translations.literal: At this time Liang had risen forty-seven years; within the borders all was calm; officials in office and gentry in the lanes rarely saw arms; when the rebels came suddenly, public and private were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had risen forty-seven years; within the borders all was calm; officials and gentry rarely saw arms; when the rebels came suddenly, public and private were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 宿將已盡，後進少年並出在外，軍旅指手為，一決於侃，侃膽力俱壯，太子深仗之。

translations.literal: Veteran generals were gone; younger successors were all abroad; the army looked to one man—Kan decided all; Kan's courage and strength were both great, and the prince relied deeply on him.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran generals were gone; younger successors were all abroad; the army looked to one man—Yang Kan decided all; his courage and strength were both great, and the prince relied deeply on him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，景至朱雀桁南，太子以臨賀王正德守宣陽門，東宮學士新野庾信守朱雀門，帥宮中文武三千餘人營桁北。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Jing reached the south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge; the prince set Prince Zhengde of Linhe to hold Xuanyang Gate, Eastern Palace scholar Yu Xin of Xinye to hold the Vermilion Bird Gate, and led more than three thousand civil and military men from the palace to camp north of the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Hou Jing reached the south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge; the prince set Prince Zhengde of Linhe to hold Xuanyang Gate, Eastern Palace scholar Yu Xin of Xinye to hold the Vermilion Bird Gate, and led more than three thousand civil and military men from the palace to camp north of the bridge.

sentences.zh: 太子命信開大桁以挫其鋒，正德曰：「百姓見開桁，必大驚駭。

translations.literal: The prince ordered Xin to open the great bridge to blunt the enemy's edge; Zhengde said, "If the people see the bridge opened, they will be greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered Xin to open the great bridge to blunt the enemy's edge; Zhengde said, "If the people see the bridge opened, they will be greatly terrified.

sentences.zh: 可且安物情。

translations.literal: We may for now settle public feeling.
translations.idiomatic: We may for now settle public feeling.

sentences.zh: 」太子從之。

translations.literal: " The prince agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而景至，信帥眾開桁，始除一舶。

translations.literal: Soon Jing arrived; Xin led his men to open the bridge, removing only one barge at first.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Jing arrived; Xin led his men to open the bridge, removing only one barge at first.

sentences.zh: 見景軍皆著鐵面，退隱於門。

translations.literal: Seeing Jing's troops all wore iron masks, he withdrew and hid behind the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Hou Jing's troops all wore iron masks, he withdrew and hid behind the gate.

sentences.zh: 信方食甘蔗，有飛箭中門柱，信手甘蔗，應弦而落，遂棄軍走。

translations.literal: Xin was eating sugarcane when a flying arrow struck the gatepost; the cane fell from his hand at the twang of the bowstring, and he abandoned his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was eating sugarcane when a flying arrow struck the gatepost; the cane fell from his hand at the twang of the bowstring, and he abandoned his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 南塘遊軍沈子睦，臨賀王正德之黨也，復閉桁渡景。

translations.literal: Shen Zimu of the South Pond patrol, a partisan of Prince Zhengde of Linhe, closed the bridge again and ferried Jing across.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zimu of the South Pond patrol, a partisan of Prince Zhengde of Linhe, closed the bridge again and ferried Hou Jing across.

sentences.zh: 太子使王質將精兵三千援信，至領軍府，遇賊，未陳而走。

translations.literal: The prince sent Wang Zhi with three thousand picked troops to aid Xin; reaching the Commandant's headquarters, they met the rebels, formed no array, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Wang Zhi with three thousand picked troops to aid Xin; reaching the Commandant's headquarters, they met the rebels, formed no array, and fled.

sentences.zh: 正德帥眾於張侯橋迎景，馬上交揖，既入宣陽門，望闕而拜，歔欷流涕，隨景渡淮。

translations.literal: Zhengde led his men to welcome Jing at Zhanghou Bridge, bowing from horseback; entering Xuanyang Gate, he looked toward the palace and bowed, weeping and sobbing, then followed Jing across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde led his men to welcome Hou Jing at Zhanghou Bridge, bowing from horseback; entering Xuanyang Gate, he looked toward the palace and bowed, weeping and sobbing, then followed him across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 景軍皆著青袍，正德軍並著絳袍，碧裡，既與景合，悉反其袍。

translations.literal: Jing's troops all wore green robes; Zhengde's all wore crimson robes with green lining; once they joined Jing, all reversed their robes.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's troops all wore green robes; Zhengde's all wore crimson robes with green lining; once they joined him, all reversed their robes.

sentences.zh: 景乘勝至闕下，城中忷懼，羊侃詐稱得射書云：「邵陵王、西昌侯援兵已至近路。

translations.literal: Jing pressed his victory to the palace gates; the city was in uproar and fear; Yang Kan falsely claimed to have received a letter shot in, saying, "Prince Lun of Shaoling and Marquis of Xichang—relief troops have reached the near road.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing pressed his victory to the palace gates; the city was in uproar and fear; Yang Kan falsely claimed to have received a letter shot in, saying, "Prince Lun of Shaoling and Marquis of Xichang—relief troops have reached the near road.

sentences.zh: 」眾乃少安。

translations.literal: " The crowd was somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd was somewhat calmed.

sentences.zh: 西豐公大春棄石頭，奔京口；

translations.literal: Duke Dachun of Xifeng abandoned Shitou and fled to Jingkou;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Dachun of Xifeng abandoned Shitou and fled to Jingkou;

sentences.zh: 謝禧、元貞棄白下走；

translations.literal: Xie Xi and Yuan Zhen abandoned Baixia and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi and Yuan Zhen abandoned Baixia and fled;

sentences.zh: 津主彭文粲等以石頭城降景，景遣其儀同三司於子悅守之。

translations.literal: Jin's commander Peng Wencan and others surrendered Shitou city to Jing; Jing sent his Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Yu Ziyue to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin's commander Peng Wencan and others surrendered Shitou city to Hou Jing; he sent Yu Ziyue, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, to hold it.

sentences.zh: 壬子，景列兵繞台城，幡旗皆黑，射啟於城中曰：「朱異等蔑弄朝權，輕作威福，臣為所陷，欲加屠戮。

translations.literal: On renzi, Jing arrayed troops around the capital enclosure; banners and flags were all black; he shot a memorial into the city, saying, "Zhu Yi and the others scorn and manipulate court power, lightly wielding authority and favor; your servant was trapped by them and faces slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Hou Jing arrayed troops around the capital enclosure; banners and flags were all black; he shot a memorial into the city, saying, "Zhu Yi and the others scorn and manipulate court power, lightly wielding authority and favor; your servant was trapped by them and faces slaughter.

sentences.zh: 陛下若誅朱異等，臣則斂轡北歸。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty executes Zhu Yi and the others, your servant will gather reins and return north.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty executes Zhu Yi and the others, your servant will gather reins and return north.

sentences.zh: 」上問太子：「有是乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked the crown prince, "Is this so?
translations.idiomatic: " The Liang emperor asked the crown prince, "Is this so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「然。

translations.literal: " He answered, "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "It is so.

sentences.zh: 」上將誅之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Liang emperor was about to execute them.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「賊以異等為名耳；

translations.literal: The prince said, "The rebels use Yi and the others only as a name;
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "The rebels use Yi and the others only as a name;

sentences.zh: 今日殺之，無救於急，適足貽笑將來，俟賊平，誅之未晚。

translations.literal: to kill them today will not help the crisis, but will only invite laughter hereafter; wait until the rebels are crushed, and execution will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: to kill them today will not help the crisis, but will only invite laughter hereafter; wait until the rebels are crushed, and execution will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Liang emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 景繞城既匝，百道俱攻，鳴鼓吹脣，喧聲震地，縱火燒大司馬、東、西華諸門。

translations.literal: Jing having encircled the city, attacked from a hundred routes, drums and horns sounded, noise shook the earth, and fire was set to the Grand Marshal and Eastern and Western Splendor gates.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing having encircled the city, attacked from a hundred routes, drums and horns sounded, noise shook the earth, and fire was set to the Grand Marshal and Eastern and Western Splendor gates.

sentences.zh: 羊侃使鑿門上為竅，下水沃火；

translations.literal: Yang Kan had holes cut in the gates above and water poured down to quench the fire;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan had holes cut in the gates above and water poured down to quench the fire;

sentences.zh: 太子自捧銀鞍，往賞戰士；

translations.literal: the prince himself carried a silver saddle to reward the warriors;
translations.idiomatic: the prince himself carried a silver saddle to reward the warriors;

sentences.zh: 直閣將軍朱思帥戰士數人逾城出外灑水，久之方滅。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant General Zhu Si led several warriors over the wall outside to pour water; only after long effort was it extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Attendant General Zhu Si led several warriors over the wall outside to pour water; only after long effort was it extinguished.

sentences.zh: 賊又以長柯斧斫東掖門，門將開，羊侃鑿扇為孔，以槊刺殺二人，斫者乃退。

translations.literal: The rebels again used long-handled axes on the Eastern Side Gate; as the gate was about to open, Yang Kan bored holes in the leaves and speared two men to death, and the choppers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again used long-handled axes on the Eastern Side Gate; as the gate was about to open, Yang Kan bored holes in the leaves and speared two men to death, and the choppers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景據公車府，正德據左衛府，景黨宋子仙據東宮，范桃棒據同泰寺。

translations.literal: Jing held the Public Chariots Office, Zhengde the Left Guard Office, Jing's partisan Song Zixian the Eastern Palace, and Fan Taobang Tongtai Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing held the Public Chariots Office, Zhengde the Left Guard Office, Song Zixian the Eastern Palace, and Fan Taobang Tongtai Temple.

sentences.zh: 景取東宮妓數百，分給軍士。

translations.literal: Jing took several hundred Eastern Palace courtesans and distributed them to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing took several hundred Eastern Palace courtesans and distributed them to the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 東宮近城，景眾登其牆射城內。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was near the wall; Jing's men climbed its ramparts and shot into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was near the wall; his men climbed its ramparts and shot into the city.

sentences.zh: 至夜，景於東宮置酒奏樂，太子遣人焚之，台殿及所聚圖書皆盡。

translations.literal: At night Jing set wine and music in the Eastern Palace; the prince sent men to burn it—the terrace halls and collected books were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: At night Hou Jing set wine and music in the Eastern Palace; the prince sent men to burn it—the terrace halls and collected books were all destroyed.

sentences.zh: 景又燒乘黃廄、士林館、太府寺。

translations.literal: Jing also burned the Imperial Horse Stable, the Forest of Scholars Hall, and the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also burned the Imperial Horse Stable, the Forest of Scholars Hall, and the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，景作木驢數百攻城，城上投石碎之。

translations.literal: On guichou, Jing built several hundred wooden siege carts; stones cast from the wall shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Hou Jing built several hundred wooden siege carts; stones cast from the wall shattered them.

sentences.zh: 景更作尖項木驢，石不能破。

translations.literal: Jing then made pointed wooden carts that stones could not break.
translations.idiomatic: He then made pointed wooden carts that stones could not break.

sentences.zh: 羊侃使作雉尾炬，灌以膏蠟，叢擲焚之，俄盡。

translations.literal: Yang Kan had pheasant-tail torches made, soaked in grease and wax, and hurled in bundles to burn them—all were soon consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan had pheasant-tail torches made, soaked in grease and wax, and hurled in bundles to burn them—all were soon consumed.

sentences.zh: 景又作登城樓，高十餘丈，欲臨射城中。

translations.literal: Jing also built siege towers more than ten zhang high, intending to overlook and shoot into the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also built siege towers more than ten zhang high, intending to overlook and shoot into the city.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「車高塹虛，彼來必倒，可臥而觀之。

translations.literal: Kan said, "The cart is high and the moat hollow—when they come they are sure to topple; we may lie down and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan said, "The cart is high and the moat hollow—when they come they are sure to topple; we may lie down and watch.

sentences.zh: 」及車動，果倒。

translations.literal: " When the cart moved, it indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: " When the cart moved, it indeed fell.

sentences.zh: 景攻既不克，士卒死傷多，乃築長圍以絕內外，又啟求誅朱異等。

translations.literal: Jing's assault having failed and his troops suffering many dead and wounded, he built a long encirclement to cut inner from outer and again memorialized asking for the execution of Zhu Yi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's assault having failed and his troops suffering many dead and wounded, he built a long encirclement to cut inner from outer and again memorialized asking for the execution of Zhu Yi and the others.

sentences.zh: 城中亦射賞格出外曰：「有能送景首者，授以景位，並錢一億萬，布絹各萬匹。

translations.literal: The city also shot a reward notice outward, saying, "Whoever can deliver Jing's head shall receive Jing's rank, plus a hundred million cash, ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The city also shot a reward notice outward, saying, "Whoever can deliver Hou Jing's head shall receive his rank, plus a hundred million cash, ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 」朱異、張綰議出兵擊之，上問羊侃，侃曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " Zhu Yi and Zhang Chuo debated sallying out to attack; the emperor asked Yang Kan, and Kan said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yi and Zhang Chuo debated sallying out to attack; the Liang emperor asked Yang Kan, and he said, "It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 今出人若少，不足破賊，徒挫銳氣；

translations.literal: If we send out too few now, we cannot break the rebels and will only blunt our keen spirit;
translations.idiomatic: If we send out too few now, we cannot break the rebels and will only blunt our keen spirit;

sentences.zh: 若多，則一旦失利，門隘橋小，必大致失亡。

translations.literal: if we send many and lose in one stroke, the gates are narrow and the bridges small—we will suffer great losses.
translations.idiomatic: if we send many and lose in one stroke, the gates are narrow and the bridges small—we will suffer great losses.

sentences.zh: 」異等不從，使千餘人出戰。

translations.literal: " Yi and the others would not listen and sent out more than a thousand men to fight.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yi and the others would not listen and sent out more than a thousand men to fight.

sentences.zh: 鋒未及交，退走，爭橋赴水死者大半。

translations.literal: Before the vanguards met, they retreated and fled; scrambling for the bridge and rushing into the water, more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the vanguards met, they retreated and fled; scrambling for the bridge and rushing into the water, more than half died.

sentences.zh: 侃子鷟，為景所獲，執至城下，以示侃，侃曰：「我傾宗報主，猶恨不足，豈計一子，幸早殺之！

translations.literal: Kan's son Zhuo was captured by Jing and brought beneath the wall to show Kan; Kan said, "I would spend my whole clan for my lord and still regret it is not enough—how would I count one son? I beg you kill him quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan's son Zhuo was captured by Hou Jing and brought beneath the wall to show him; Yang Kan said, "I would spend my whole clan for my lord and still regret it is not enough—how would I count one son? I beg you kill him quickly!

sentences.zh: 」數日，復持來，侃謂鷟曰：「久以汝為死矣，猶在邪！

translations.literal: " After several days they brought him again; Kan said to Zhuo, "I had long thought you dead—still alive!
translations.idiomatic: " After several days they brought him again; Yang Kan said to Zhuo, "I had long thought you dead—still alive!

sentences.zh: 」引弓射之。

translations.literal: " He drew his bow and shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his bow and shot at him.

sentences.zh: 景以其忠義，亦不之殺。

translations.literal: Jing, because of his loyalty and righteousness, did not kill him either.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, because of his loyalty and righteousness, did not kill him either.

sentences.zh: 莊鐵慮景不克，托稱迎母，與左右數十人趣歷陽。

translations.literal: Zhuang Tie, fearing Jing would not prevail, claimed he was going to fetch his mother and hurried to Liyang with several dozen followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Tie, fearing Hou Jing would not prevail, claimed he was going to fetch his mother and hurried to Liyang with several dozen followers.

sentences.zh: 先遣書紿田英、郭駱曰：「侯王已為台軍所殺，國家使我歸鎮。

translations.literal: He first sent a letter deceiving Tian Ying and Guo Luo, saying, "The Prince of Hou has been killed by imperial troops; the state sends me back to my post.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent a letter deceiving Tian Ying and Guo Luo, saying, "The Prince of Hou has been killed by imperial troops; the state sends me back to my post.

sentences.zh: 」駱等大懼，棄城奔壽陽，鐵入城，不敢守，奉其母奔尋陽。

translations.literal: " Luo and the others were greatly afraid, abandoned the city, and fled to Shouyang; Tie entered the city, dared not hold it, and took his mother to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Luo and the others were greatly afraid, abandoned the city, and fled to Shouyang; Tie entered the city, dared not hold it, and took his mother to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊午朔，刑白馬，祀蚩尤於太極殿前。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day wuwu, a white horse was sacrificed and Chiyou worshipped before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day wuwu, a white horse was sacrificed and Chiyou worshipped before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 臨賀王正德即帝位於儀賢堂，下詔稱：「普通已來，奸邪亂政，上久不豫，社稷將危。

translations.literal: Prince Zhengde of Linhe took the throne in the Hall of Worthy Rites and issued an edict, saying, "Since the Putong era wicked men have disordered government; the emperor has long been unwell and the altars of state are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhengde of Linhe took the throne in the Hall of Worthy Rites and issued an edict, saying, "Since the Putong era wicked men have disordered government; the emperor has long been unwell and the altars of state are in peril.

sentences.zh: 河南王景，釋位來朝，猥用朕躬，紹茲寶位，可大赦，改元正平。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Henan, relinquishing his post to come to court, has unworthily used Our person to continue this precious throne; a general amnesty is proclaimed and the era is changed to Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Henan, relinquishing his post to come to court, has unworthily used Our person to continue this precious throne; a general amnesty is proclaimed and the era is changed to Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 」立其世子見理為皇太子，以景為丞相，妻以女，並出家之寶貨悉助軍費。

translations.literal: " He made his heir Jianli crown prince, made Jing chancellor, gave him his daughter in marriage, and contributed all the family's treasures to military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: " He made his heir Jianli crown prince, made Hou Jing chancellor, gave him his daughter in marriage, and contributed all the family's treasures to military expenses.

sentences.zh: 於是景營於闕前，分其兵二千人攻東府；

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing encamped before the palace gates and sent two thousand of his troops to attack the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Hou Jing encamped before the palace gates and sent two thousand of his troops to attack the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 南浦侯推拒之，三日，不克。

translations.literal: Marquis Tui of Nanpu resisted; three days passed without success.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Tui of Nanpu resisted; three days passed without success.

sentences.zh: 景自往攻之，矢石雨下，宣城王防閤許伯眾潛引景眾登城。

translations.literal: Jing went to attack in person; arrows and stones fell like rain; Xu Bojhong, gate guard of Prince Xuancheng, secretly led Jing's men onto the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing went to attack in person; arrows and stones fell like rain; Xu Bojhong, gate guard of Prince Xuancheng, secretly led his men onto the wall.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，克之；

translations.literal: On xinyou, it was taken;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, it was taken;

sentences.zh: 殺南浦侯推及城中戰士三千人，載其屍聚於杜姥宅，遙語城中人曰：「若不早降，正當如此！

translations.literal: Marquis Tui of Nanpu and three thousand warriors in the city were killed; their corpses were loaded and piled at Old Du's house, and they shouted to the city, "If you do not surrender soon, this is exactly what awaits!
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Tui of Nanpu and three thousand warriors in the city were killed; their corpses were piled at Old Du's house, and they shouted to the city, "If you do not surrender soon, this is exactly what awaits!

sentences.zh: 景聲言上已晏駕，雖城中亦以為然。

translations.literal: Jing spread word that the emperor had already died; even within the city many believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing spread word that the Liang emperor had already died; even within the city many believed it.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，太子請上巡城，上幸大司馬門，城上聞蹕聲，皆鼓噪流涕，眾心粗安。

translations.literal: On renxu, the prince asked the emperor to inspect the walls; the emperor went to the Grand Marshal Gate; hearing the imperial procession on the wall, all cheered and wept, and public feeling was somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the prince asked the Liang emperor to inspect the walls; he went to the Grand Marshal Gate; hearing the imperial procession on the wall, all cheered and wept, and public feeling was somewhat calmed.

sentences.zh: 江子一之敗還也，上責之。

translations.literal: When Jiang Ziyi returned defeated, the emperor rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ziyi returned defeated, the Liang emperor rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 子一拜謝曰：「臣以身許國，常恐不得其死；

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed and said, "Your servant pledged his body to the state and always feared he would not find death;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi bowed and said, "Your servant pledged his body to the state and always feared he would not find death;

sentences.zh: 今所部皆棄臣去，臣以一夫安能擊賊！

translations.literal: now my command has all abandoned me—how can one man strike the rebels!
translations.idiomatic: now my command has all abandoned me—how can one man strike the rebels!

sentences.zh: 若賊遂能至此，臣誓當碎身以贖前罪，不死闕前，當死闕後。

translations.literal: If the rebels can reach this far, your servant vows to shatter his body to atone for past fault—if not dead before the gate, then dead behind it.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels can reach this far, your servant vows to shatter his body to atone for past fault—if not dead before the gate, then dead behind it.

sentences.zh: 」乙亥，子一啟太子，與弟尚書左丞子四、東宮主帥子五帥所領百餘人開承明門出戰。

translations.literal: " On yihai, Ziyi reported to the prince and, with his brothers Left Assistant Minister Zisi and Eastern Palace commander Ziwu, led more than a hundred men under their command out through Chenming Gate to fight.
translations.idiomatic: " On yihai, Ziyi reported to the prince and, with his brothers Left Assistant Minister Zisi and Eastern Palace commander Ziwu, led more than a hundred men under their command out through Chenming Gate to fight.

sentences.zh: 子一直抵賊營，賊伏兵不動。

translations.literal: Ziyi went straight to the rebel camp; the ambush did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi went straight to the rebel camp; the ambush did not stir.

sentences.zh: 子一呼曰：「賊輩何不速出！

translations.literal: Ziyi shouted, "Rebels, why not come out quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi shouted, "Rebels, why not come out quickly!

sentences.zh: 」久之，賊騎出，夾攻之。

translations.literal: " After long delay rebel cavalry came out and attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: " After long delay rebel cavalry came out and attacked from both sides.

sentences.zh: 子一徑前，引槊刺賊；

translations.literal: Ziyi went straight forward and thrust his spear at the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi went straight forward and thrust his spear at the rebels;

sentences.zh: 從者莫敢繼，賊解其肩而死。

translations.literal: none of his followers dared follow; the rebels cut off his shoulder and he died.
translations.idiomatic: none of his followers dared follow; the rebels cut off his shoulder and he died.

sentences.zh: 子四、子五相謂曰：「與兄俱出，何面獨旋！

translations.literal: Zisi and Ziwu said to each other, "We came out with our brother—what face have we to return alone!
translations.idiomatic: Zisi and Ziwu said to each other, "We came out with our brother—what face have we to return alone!

sentences.zh: 」皆免冑赴賊。

translations.literal: " Both removed their helmets and rushed at the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " Both removed their helmets and rushed at the rebels.

sentences.zh: 子四中槊，洞胸而死；

translations.literal: Zisi was speared, pierced through the chest, and died;
translations.idiomatic: Zisi was speared, pierced through the chest, and died;

sentences.zh: 子五傷脰，還至塹，一慟而絕。

translations.literal: Ziwu was wounded in the neck; returning to the moat, he gave one sob and expired.
translations.idiomatic: Ziwu was wounded in the neck; returning to the moat, he gave one sob and expired.

sentences.zh: 景初至建康，謂朝夕可拔，號令嚴整，士卒不敢侵暴。

translations.literal: When Jing first reached Jiankang, he thought the city could be taken within days; his orders were strict and soldiers dared not loot.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing first reached Jiankang, he thought the city could be taken within days; his orders were strict and soldiers dared not loot.

sentences.zh: 及屢攻不克，人心離沮。

translations.literal: After repeated assaults failed, hearts turned away and spirits sank.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated assaults failed, hearts turned away and spirits sank.

sentences.zh: 景恐援兵四集，一旦潰去；

translations.literal: Jing feared relief troops would gather from four sides and he would collapse in a day;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing feared relief troops would gather from four sides and he would collapse in a day;

sentences.zh: 又食石頭常平諸倉既盡，軍中乏食；

translations.literal: also the Shitou and Changping granaries were exhausted and the army lacked food;
translations.idiomatic: also the Shitou and Changping granaries were exhausted and the army lacked food;

sentences.zh: 乃縱士卒掠奪民米及金帛子女。

translations.literal: he then let soldiers plunder the people's grain, gold, silk, and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: he then let soldiers plunder the people's grain, gold, silk, and daughters.

sentences.zh: 是後米一升直七八萬錢，人相食，餓死者什五六。

translations.literal: After this one sheng of rice cost seven or eight hundred thousand cash; men ate one another; five or six in ten died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: After this one sheng of rice cost seven or eight hundred thousand cash; men ate one another; five or six in ten died of hunger.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，景於城東、西起土山，驅迫士民，不限貴賤，亂加毆捶，疲羸者因殺以填山，號哭動地。

translations.literal: On yichou, Jing raised earthen hills east and west of the city, driving commoners and gentry without distinction of rank, beating them at random; the weak and wasted were killed to fill the hills—wailing shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Hou Jing raised earthen hills east and west of the city, driving commoners and gentry without distinction of rank, beating them at random; the weak and wasted were killed to fill the hills—wailing shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 民不敢竄匿，並出從之，旬日間，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: The people dared not hide and all came out to follow; within ten days the crowd reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The people dared not hide and all came out to follow; within ten days the crowd reached tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 城中亦築土山以應之。

translations.literal: Within the city they also built earthen hills in response.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city they also built earthen hills in response.

sentences.zh: 太子、宣城王已下，皆親負土，執畚鍤，於山上起芙蓉層樓，高四丈，飾以錦罽，募敢死士二千人，厚衣袍鎧，謂之「僧騰客」，分配二山，晝夜交戰不息。

translations.literal: From the prince and Prince Xuancheng downward, all personally carried earth and wielded spades; on the hills they raised lotus-layered towers four zhang high, adorned with brocade; two thousand dare-to-die men were recruited, heavily clad in robes and armor, called "Monk Soarers"; they were assigned to both hills and fought day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the prince and Prince Xuancheng downward, all personally carried earth and wielded spades; on the hills they raised lotus-layered towers four zhang high, adorned with brocade; two thousand dare-to-die men were recruited, heavily clad in robes and armor, called "Monk Soarers"; they were assigned to both hills and fought day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，城內土山崩；

translations.literal: Heavy rain came; the inner earthen hill collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain came; the inner earthen hill collapsed;

sentences.zh: 賊乘之，垂入，苦戰不能禁。

translations.literal: the rebels seized the moment and nearly entered; bitter fighting could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels seized the moment and nearly entered; bitter fighting could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 羊侃令多擲火，為火城以斷其路，徐於內築城，賊不能進。

translations.literal: Yang Kan ordered much fire cast down, made a fire wall to cut their path, and slowly built a wall within; the rebels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan ordered much fire cast down, made a fire wall to cut their path, and slowly built a wall within; the rebels could not advance.

sentences.zh: 景募人奴降者，悉免為良；

translations.literal: Jing recruited household slaves who surrendered and freed them all as commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing recruited household slaves who surrendered and freed them all as commoners;

sentences.zh: 得朱異奴，以為儀同三司，異家資產悉與之。

translations.literal: obtaining Zhu Yi's slave, he made him Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and gave him all of Yi's family property.
translations.idiomatic: obtaining Zhu Yi's slave, he made him Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and gave him all of Yi's family property.

sentences.zh: 奴乘良馬，衣錦袍，於城下仰詬異曰：「汝五十年仕宦，方得中領軍；

translations.literal: The slave rode a fine horse and wore a brocade robe; beneath the wall he looked up and cursed Yi, saying, "You served fifty years in office and only then became Central Army Commander;
translations.idiomatic: The slave rode a fine horse and wore a brocade robe; beneath the wall he looked up and cursed Zhu Yi, saying, "You served fifty years in office and only then became Central Army Commander;

sentences.zh: 我始事侯王，已為儀同矣！

translations.literal: I have only just begun serving the Prince of Hou and am already Equal in Honor!
translations.idiomatic: I have only just begun serving the Prince of Hou and am already Equal in Honor!

sentences.zh: 」於是三日之中，群奴出就景者以千數，景皆厚撫以配軍，人人感恩，為之致死。

translations.literal: " Within three days slaves who went over to Jing numbered in the thousands; Jing treated them all generously and assigned them to the army; each man was grateful and fought to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: " Within three days slaves who went over to Hou Jing numbered in the thousands; he treated them all generously and assigned them to the army; each man was grateful and fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史湘東王繹聞景圍台城，丙寅，戒嚴，移檄所督湘州刺史河東王譽、雍州刺史岳陽王察、江州刺史當陽公大心、郢州刺史南平王恪等，發兵入援。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yi of Xiangdong, hearing Jing had besieged the capital enclosure, on bingyin ordered martial law and sent proclamations to those under his command—Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yu of Hedong, Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang, Jiangzhou Inspector Duke Daxin of Dangyang, Yingzhou Inspector Prince Ke of Nanping, and others—to raise troops and march to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yi of Xiangdong, hearing Hou Jing had besieged the capital enclosure, on bingyin ordered martial law and sent proclamations to those under his command—Jingzhou Inspector Prince Yu of Hedong, Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang, Jiangzhou Inspector Duke Daxin of Dangyang, Yingzhou Inspector Prince Ke of Nanping, and others—to raise troops and march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 大心，大器之弟；

translations.literal: Daxin was the younger brother of Daqi.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin was the younger brother of Daqi.

sentences.zh: 恪，偉之子也。

translations.literal: Ke was Wei's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was Wei's son.

sentences.zh: 朱異遺景書，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi sent Jing a letter explaining fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi sent Hou Jing a letter explaining fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 景報書，並告城中士民，以為：「梁自近歲以來，權幸用事，割剝齊民，以供嗜欲。

translations.literal: Jing replied and also addressed the gentry and people in the city, saying, "In recent years Liang has been ruled by favorites who strip the common people to feed their appetites.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing replied and also addressed the gentry and people in the city, saying, "In recent years Liang has been ruled by favorites who strip the common people to feed their appetites.

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，公等試觀：今日國家池苑，王公第宅，僧尼寺塔；

translations.literal: If you say this is not so, gentlemen, look: today's state pools and parks, princes' mansions, monks' and nuns' temples and pagodas;
translations.idiomatic: If you say this is not so, gentlemen, look: today's state pools and parks, princes' mansions, monks' and nuns' temples and pagodas;

sentences.zh: 及在位庶僚，姬姜百室，僕從數千，不耕不織，錦衣玉食；

translations.literal: and officials in office, concubines filling a hundred chambers, retainers numbering thousands—neither plowing nor weaving, yet brocade robes and jade fare;
translations.idiomatic: and officials in office, concubines filling a hundred chambers, retainers numbering thousands—neither plowing nor weaving, yet brocade robes and jade fare;

sentences.zh: 不奪百姓，從何得之！

translations.literal: if they do not seize from the common people, whence do they obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: if they do not seize from the common people, whence do they obtain it!

sentences.zh: 僕所以趨赴闕庭，指誅權佞，非傾社稷。

translations.literal: Your servant hurries to the court gate to execute the power-holders—not to overturn the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hurries to the court gate to execute the power-holders—not to overturn the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 今城中指望四方入援，吾觀王侯、諸將，志在全身，誰能竭力致死，與吾爭勝負哉！

translations.literal: Now within the city you look to relief from four directions; I see princes and generals whose aim is to save themselves—who will exhaust his strength and die fighting to contend victory and defeat with me!
translations.idiomatic: Now within the city you look to relief from four directions; I see princes and generals whose aim is to save themselves—who will exhaust his strength and die fighting to contend victory and defeat with me!

sentences.zh: 長江天險，二曹所歎，吾一葦航之，日明氣淨。

translations.literal: The Yangtze is heaven's barrier, what the two Caos lamented—I crossed it on a single reed, under bright sun and clear air.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze's natural fortifications made Cao Cao and Cao Pi sigh—I crossed it on a reed boat, under bright sun and clear air.

sentences.zh: 自非天人允協，何能如是！

translations.literal: Unless heaven and men were in accord, how could it be so!
translations.idiomatic: Unless heaven and men were in accord, how could such a thing happen!

sentences.zh: 幸各三思，自求元吉！

translations.literal: I hope each of you will think thrice and seek your own great fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully, each of you, and seek your own fortune!

sentences.zh: 景又奉啟於東魏主，稱：「臣進取壽春，暫欲停憩。

translations.literal: Jing also submitted a memorial to the Eastern Wei ruler, saying, "Your servant advanced on Shouchun intending to halt and rest awhile.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing also submitted a memorial to the Eastern Wei emperor, saying, "Your servant advanced on Shouchun intending to halt and rest awhile.

sentences.zh: 而蕭衍識此運終，自辭寶位；

translations.literal: But Xiao Yan perceived this fate was ending and resigned the imperial seat himself;
translations.idiomatic: But Xiao Yan perceived his fate was ending and resigned the throne himself;

sentences.zh: 臣軍未入其國，已投同泰捨身。

translations.literal: before your servant's army entered his state, he had already gone to Tongtai Temple to relinquish his body.
translations.idiomatic: before your servant's army entered his realm, he had already gone to Tongtai Temple to renounce the throne.

sentences.zh: 去月二十九日，屆此建康。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth of last month, I arrived at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth of last month, I arrived at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 江海未蘇，干戈暫止，永言故鄉，人馬同戀。

translations.literal: Rivers and seas are not yet calmed, weapons have briefly ceased—ever thinking of home, men and horses alike long for it.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and seas are not yet calmed, arms have briefly ceased—I long for home, as do my men and horses.

sentences.zh: 尋當整轡，以奉聖顏。

translations.literal: Soon I shall rein in and return to pay homage to Your Majesty's face.
translations.idiomatic: Soon I shall turn home to pay homage to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣之母、弟，久謂屠滅，近奉明敕，始承猶在。

translations.literal: Your servant's mother and younger brother, long thought slaughtered, by recent clear edict I first learn they still live.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's mother and brother, long thought dead, I have just learned by edict that they still live.

sentences.zh: 斯乃陛下寬仁，大將軍恩念，臣之弱劣，知何仰報！

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty's breadth and mercy, the Grand General's kindness—your servant is weak and lowly, how can I repay such favor!
translations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty's mercy and the Grand General's kindness—your servant is weak and lowly; how can I repay it!

sentences.zh: 今輒繼啟迎臣母、弟、妻、兒，伏願聖慈，特賜裁放！

translations.literal: Now I humbly submit again asking to receive my mother, brother, wife, and children—I prostrate myself, hoping for Your Majesty's holy compassion to grant release!
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask again that my mother, brother, wife, and children be released—I prostrate myself, hoping Your Majesty will grant it!

sentences.zh: 己巳，湘東王繹遣司馬吳曄、天門太守樊文皎等將兵發江陵。

translations.literal: On jisi, Prince of Xiangdong Yi dispatched Staff Officer Wu Ye, Tiantai prefect Fan Wenjiao, and others leading troops from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong dispatched staff officer Wu Ye, Tiantai prefect Fan Wenjiao, and others with troops from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 陳昕為景所擒，景與之極飲，使昕收集部曲，欲用之。

translations.literal: Chen Xin was captured by Jing; Jing drank heavily with him and had Xin gather his followers, intending to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin was captured by Hou Jing; Jing drank heavily with him and had Xin gather his followers, intending to employ him.

sentences.zh: 昕不可，景使其儀同三司范桃棒囚之。

translations.literal: Xin refused; Jing had his Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Fan Taobang imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin refused; Jing had Fan Taobang, Equal to the Three Dukes, imprison him.

sentences.zh: 昕因說桃棒，使帥所部襲殺王偉、宋子仙，詣城降。

translations.literal: Xin then persuaded Taobang to lead his troops in a surprise attack to kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian and surrender to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then persuaded Taobang to lead his troops in a surprise attack on Wang Wei and Song Zixian, then surrender to the city.

sentences.zh: 桃棒從之，潛遣昕夜縋入城。

translations.literal: Taobang agreed and secretly sent Xin by rope into the city at night.
translations.idiomatic: Taobang agreed and secretly sent Xin over the wall into the city by night.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，敕鐫銀券賜桃棒曰：「事定之日，封汝河南王，即有景眾，並給金帛女樂。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered a silver tally engraved and given to Taobang, saying, "When affairs are settled, you shall be made Prince of Henan; Hou Jing's troops shall be yours, with gold, silk, and female musicians besides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered a silver tally for Taobang: "When this is settled, you shall be Prince of Henan; Hou Jing's troops will be yours, along with gold, silk, and musicians.

sentences.zh: 」太子恐其詐，猶豫不決，上怒曰：「受降常理，何忽致疑！

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince feared deception and hesitated; the emperor angrily said, "Accepting surrender is common sense—why suddenly doubt it!
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince feared a ruse and hesitated; the emperor angrily said, "Accepting surrender is common sense—why doubt it now!

sentences.zh: 」太子召公卿會議，朱異、傅岐曰：「桃棒降必非謬。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince summoned ministers to confer; Zhu Yi and Fu Qi said, "Taobang's surrender cannot be false.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince summoned ministers to confer; Zhu Yi and Fu Qi said, "Taobang's surrender cannot be false.

sentences.zh: 桃棒既降，賊景必驚，乘此擊之，可大破也。

translations.literal: Once Taobang has surrendered, the rebel Jing will surely be alarmed; strike now and he can be greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taobang surrenders, Hou Jing will be alarmed; strike now and we can break him utterly.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「吾堅城自守以俟外援，援兵既至，賊豈足平！

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince said, "I will hold the walls and wait for outside aid; when relief arrives, will the rebels not be easily crushed!
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said, "I will hold the walls and wait for relief; when reinforcements arrive, will the rebels not be easily crushed!

sentences.zh: 此萬全策也。

translations.literal: This is the completely safe plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is the safest course.

sentences.zh: 今開門納桃棒，桃棒之情，何易可知！

translations.literal: To open the gates now and admit Taobang—how easily can his intentions be known!
translations.idiomatic: To open the gates and admit Taobang now—how can we know his true intent!

sentences.zh: 萬一為變，悔無所及。

translations.literal: If by chance there is treachery, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If he turns on us, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 社稷事重，須更詳之。

translations.literal: The fate of the state is grave—it must be considered further.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the state hangs on this—it must be weighed more carefully.

sentences.zh: 」異曰：「殿下若以社稷之急，宜納桃棒；

translations.literal: " Yi said, "If Your Highness considers the state's emergency, Taobang should be admitted;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yi said, "If Your Highness weighs the state's emergency, Taobang should be admitted;

sentences.zh: 如其猶豫，非異所知。

translations.literal: if you hesitate, that is beyond what Yi can know.
translations.idiomatic: if you hesitate, I cannot advise further.

sentences.zh: 」太子終不能決。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince could not decide in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince could not decide.

sentences.zh: 桃棒又使昕啟曰：「今止將所領五百人，若至城門，皆自脫甲，乞朝廷開門賜容。

translations.literal: Taobang again had Xin report: "I will bring only five hundred men; at the gate they will all remove their armor—I beg the court to open and grant entry.
translations.idiomatic: Taobang sent Xin again: "I will bring only five hundred men; at the gate they will remove their armor—I beg the court to open and admit us.

sentences.zh: 事濟之後，保擒侯景。

translations.literal: Once the affair succeeds, I guarantee to capture Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When it is done, I guarantee to capture Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 」太子見其懇切，愈疑之。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince saw how earnest it was and grew more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince saw how earnest it was and grew more suspicious.

sentences.zh: 朱異拊膺曰：「失此，社稷事去矣！

translations.literal: Zhu Yi beat his breast and said, "Miss this chance and the state is lost!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi beat his breast: "Miss this chance and the state is lost!

sentences.zh: 」俄而桃棒為部下所告，景拉殺之。

translations.literal: " Shortly Taobang was reported by his subordinates; Jing had him torn apart and killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Taobang was betrayed by his own men; Jing had him torn apart and killed.

sentences.zh: 陳昕不知，如期而出，景邀得之，逼使射書城中曰：「桃棒且輕將數十人先入。

translations.literal: Chen Xin did not know; he came out as agreed; Jing intercepted and seized him, forced him to shoot a letter into the city saying, "Taobang will first enter lightly with several dozen men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin, knowing nothing, came out as agreed; Jing intercepted him and forced him to shoot a letter into the city: "Taobang will enter first with a small party.

sentences.zh: 」景欲衷甲隨之，昕不肯，期以必死，乃殺之。

translations.literal: " Jing wished to follow in hidden armor; Xin refused, vowing to die—so Jing killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing wished to follow in hidden armor; Xin refused, preferring death—so Jing killed him.

sentences.zh: 景使蕭見理與儀同三司盧暉略戍東府。

translations.literal: Jing had Xiao Jianli and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Lu Huilue garrison the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing posted Xiao Jianli and Lu Huilue, Equal to the Three Dukes, at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 見理凶險，夜，與群盜剽劫於大桁，中流矢而死。

translations.literal: Jianli was fierce and dangerous; at night he robbed with bandits at the Great Bridge and was struck by an arrow and died midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli was fierce and violent; by night he plundered with bandits at the Great Bridge and was struck by an arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸行至鐘離，聞侯景已渡採石，綸晝夜兼道，旋軍入援，濟江，中流風起，人馬溺者什一二。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun had reached Zhongli; hearing Hou Jing had crossed Caishi, Lun traveled day and night by double stages, turned his army to aid, crossed the river—midstream wind rose, one or two in ten of men and horses drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Lun of Shaoling had reached Zhongli; hearing Hou Jing had crossed Caishi, he raced day and night to relieve the city, crossed the Yangtze—a sudden wind midstream drowned one or two men in ten.

sentences.zh: 遂帥寧遠將軍西豐公大春、新淦公大成、永安侯確、安南侯駿、前譙州刺史趙伯超、武州刺史蕭弄璋等，步騎三萬，自京口西上。

translations.literal: He then led Ningyuan General Prince of Xifeng Dachun, Prince of Xingan Dacheng, Marquis of Yong'an Que, Marquis of Annan Jun, former Qiaozhou Inspector Zhao Bochao, Wuzhou Inspector Xiao Nongzhang, and others—thirty thousand foot and horse—from Jingkou westward.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Ningyuan general Prince Dachun of Xifeng, Prince Dacheng of Xingan, Marquis Que of Yong'an, Marquis Jun of Annan, former Qiaozhou inspector Zhao Bochao, Wuzhou inspector Xiao Nongzhang, and others—thirty thousand infantry and cavalry—from Jingkou westward.

sentences.zh: 大成，大春之弟；

translations.literal: Dacheng was Dachun's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was Dachun's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 確，綸之子；

translations.literal: Que was Lun's son;
translations.idiomatic: Que was Lun's son;

sentences.zh: 駿，懿之孫也。

translations.literal: Jun was Yi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was the grandson of Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 景遣軍至江乘拒綸軍。

translations.literal: Jing dispatched troops to Jiangcheng to block Lun's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jing dispatched troops to Jiangcheng to block Lun's army.

sentences.zh: 趙伯超曰：「若從黃城大路，必與賊遇，不如徑指鐘山，突據廣莫門。

translations.literal: Zhao Bochao said, "If we take the Huangcheng main road, we will surely meet the rebels; better to strike straight for Zhong Mountain and seize Guangmo Gate by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bochao said, "If we take the Huangcheng main road, we will meet the rebels; better to strike straight for Zhong Mountain and seize Guangmo Gate by surprise.

sentences.zh: 出賊不意，城圍必解矣。

translations.literal: Catching the rebels off guard, the siege will surely be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Catching the rebels off guard, the siege will surely be lifted.

sentences.zh: 」綸從之，夜行失道，迂二十餘里。

translations.literal: " Lun agreed, marched by night, lost the way, and went twenty-odd li out of course.
translations.idiomatic: " Lun agreed, marched by night, lost the way, and went twenty-odd li out of course.

sentences.zh: 庚辰旦，營於蔣山。

translations.literal: At dawn on gengchen, he encamped on Mount Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on gengchen, he encamped on Mount Jiang.

sentences.zh: 景見之大駭，悉送所掠婦女、珍貨於石頭，具舟欲走。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly alarmed at the sight; he sent all plundered women and treasures to Shitou, prepared boats, and intended to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was greatly alarmed; he sent all plundered women and treasures to Shitou, prepared boats, and intended to flee.

sentences.zh: 分兵三道攻綸，綸與戰，破之。

translations.literal: He divided his army in three paths to attack Lun; Lun fought and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his army in three columns to attack Lun; Lun fought and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 時山巔寒雪，乃引軍下愛敬寺。

translations.literal: Cold snow lay on the mountain peaks; he then led his army down to Aijing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cold snow lay on the peaks; he led his army down to Aijing Temple.

sentences.zh: 景陳兵於覆舟山北，乙酉，綸進軍玄武湖側，與景對陳，不戰。

translations.literal: Jing arrayed troops north of Fuzhou Mountain; on yiyou, Lun advanced to the side of Xuanwu Lake and faced Jing's array without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Jing arrayed troops north of Fuzhou Mountain; on yiyou, Lun advanced to Xuanwu Lake and faced Jing's line without fighting.

sentences.zh: 至暮，景更約明日會戰，綸許之。

translations.literal: At dusk, Jing proposed battle again the next day; Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, Jing proposed battle again the next day; Lun agreed.

sentences.zh: 安南侯駿見景軍退，以為走，即與壯士逐之；

translations.literal: Marquis of Annan Jun saw Jing's army retreat and thought they were fleeing; he immediately pursued with stalwart men;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jun of Annan saw Jing's army retreat and thought they were fleeing; he immediately pursued with picked men;

sentences.zh: 景旋軍擊之，駿敗走，趣綸軍。

translations.literal: Jing wheeled his army and struck; Jun was defeated and fled toward Lun's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wheeled his army and struck; Jun was defeated and fled toward Lun's army.

sentences.zh: 趙伯超望見，亦引兵走，景乘勝追擊之，諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: Zhao Bochao saw it from afar and also led his troops away; Jing pressed the victory in pursuit and all armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bochao saw it from afar and also fled; Jing pressed the victory and all armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 綸收餘兵近千人，入天保寺；

translations.literal: Lun gathered nearly a thousand remaining soldiers and entered Tianbao Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Lun gathered nearly a thousand survivors and entered Tianbao Temple;

sentences.zh: 景追之，縱火燒寺。

translations.literal: Jing pursued and set fire to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pursued and set fire to the temple.

sentences.zh: 綸奔朱方，士卒踐冰雪，往往墮足。

translations.literal: Lun fled to Zhufang; soldiers treading ice and snow often lost their footing.
translations.idiomatic: Lun fled to Zhufang; soldiers treading ice and snow often lost their footing.

sentences.zh: 景悉收綸輜重，生擒西豐公大春、安前司馬莊丘慧、主帥霍俊等而還。

translations.literal: Jing seized all of Lun's baggage, captured alive Prince of Xifeng Dachun, former Annan staff officer Zhuang Qiu Hui, commander Huo Jun, and others, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jing seized all of Lun's baggage, captured Prince Dachun of Xifeng, former Annan staff officer Zhuang Qiu Hui, commander Huo Jun, and others alive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，景陳所獲綸軍首虜鎧仗及大春等於城下，使言曰：「邵陵王已為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Jing displayed the heads, captives, armor, and weapons taken from Lun's army and Dachun and the rest below the walls, and had it said, "Prince of Shaoling has been killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Jing displayed the heads, captives, armor, and weapons taken from Lun's army and Dachun and the rest below the walls, and had it said, "Prince Shaoling has been killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」霍俊獨曰：「王小失利，已全軍還京口。

translations.literal: " Huo Jun alone said, "The prince suffered a small setback and has already returned with his whole army to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " Huo Jun alone said, "The prince suffered a small setback and has already returned with his whole army to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 城中但堅守，援軍尋至。

translations.literal: Hold the city firm—relief will soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the city firm—relief will soon arrive.

sentences.zh: 」賊以刀毆其背，俊辭色彌厲；

translations.literal: " The rebels beat his back with blades; Jun's words and bearing grew fiercer;
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels beat his back with blades; Jun's words and bearing grew fiercer;

sentences.zh: 景義而釋之，臨賀王正德殺之。

translations.literal: Jing admired his loyalty and released him; Prince of Linhe Zhengde killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing admired his loyalty and released him; Prince Zhengde of Linhe killed him.

sentences.zh: 是日晚，鄱陽王范遣其世子嗣與西豫州刺史裴之高、建安太守趙鳳舉各將兵入援，軍於蔡洲，以待上流諸軍，范以之高督江右援軍事。

translations.literal: That same evening, Prince of Poyang Fan sent his heir Si, Western Yuzhou Inspector Pei Zhigao, and Jian'an prefect Zhao Fengju each leading troops to aid, encamping at Caizhou to await upstream armies; Fan made Zhigao commander of relief forces on the river's right.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening, Prince Xiao Fan of Poyang sent his heir Si, Western Yuzhou inspector Pei Zhigao, and Jian'an prefect Zhao Fengju each with relief troops, encamping at Caizhou to await upstream armies; Fan made Zhigao commander of relief forces west of the river.

sentences.zh: 景悉驅南岸居民於水北，焚其廬舍，大街已西，掃地俱盡。

translations.literal: Jing drove all residents of the south bank to the north of the water, burned their dwellings, and west of the main street swept the ground clean of everything.
translations.idiomatic: Jing drove all residents of the south bank to the north side, burned their dwellings, and west of the main street swept everything bare.

sentences.zh: 北徐州刺史封山侯正表鎮鐘離，上召之入援，正表托以船糧未集，不進。

translations.literal: Northern Xuzhou Inspector Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao held Zhongli; the emperor summoned him to aid, but Zhengbiao pleaded that boats and grain were not yet assembled and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Xuzhou inspector Marquis Zhengbiao of Fengshan held Zhongli; the emperor summoned him to aid, but Zhengbiao pleaded that boats and grain were not ready and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 景以正表為南兗州刺史，封南郡王。

translations.literal: Jing made Zhengbiao Southern Yanzhou Inspector and enfeoffed him as Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Zhengbiao Southern Yanzhou inspector and enfeoffed him as Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 正表乃於歐陽立柵以斷援軍，帥眾一萬，聲言入援，實欲襲廣陵。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao then built a stockade at Ouyang to cut off relief armies, leading ten thousand men under the claim of coming to aid but actually intending to strike Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao then built a stockade at Ouyang to cut off relief armies, leading ten thousand men under the claim of coming to aid but actually intending to strike Guangling.

sentences.zh: 密書誘廣陵令劉詢，使燒城為應，詢以告南兗州刺史南康王會理。

translations.literal: He sent secret letters to entice Guangling magistrate Liu Xun to burn the city as signal; Xun reported this to Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince of Nankang Huili.
translations.idiomatic: He sent secret letters to entice Guangling magistrate Liu Xun to burn the city as signal; Xun reported this to Southern Yanzhou inspector Prince Huili of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，會理使詢帥步騎千人夜襲正表，大破之；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huili had Xun lead a thousand foot and horse in a night attack on Zhengbiao and routed him;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Huili had Xun lead a thousand infantry and cavalry in a night attack on Zhengbiao and routed him;

sentences.zh: 正表走還鐘離。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao fled back to Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao fled back to Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 詢收其兵糧，歸就會理，與之入援。

translations.literal: Xun seized his arms and grain, returned to join Huili, and entered to aid with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun seized his arms and grain, rejoined Huili, and marched to relieve the city with him.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，侍中、都官尚書羊侃卒，城中益懼。

translations.literal: On guisi, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Justice Yang Kan died; fear in the city increased.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, attendant-in-ordinary and minister of justice Yang Kan died; fear in the city deepened.

sentences.zh: 侯景大造攻具，陳於闕前，大車高數丈，一車二十輪。

translations.literal: Hou Jing greatly built siege engines and arrayed them before the palace gate—great carts several zhang high, twenty wheels to a cart.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing built great siege engines and arrayed them before the palace gate—carts several zhang high, twenty wheels each.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，復進攻城，以蝦蟆車運土填塹。

translations.literal: On dingyou, he again advanced to attack the city, using toad carts to haul earth and fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, he again attacked the city, using toad carts to haul earth and fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹遣世子方等將步騎一萬入援建康，庚子，發公安。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent his heir Fangdeng leading ten thousand foot and horse to aid Jiankang; on gengzi they set out from Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent his heir Fangdeng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to aid Jiankang; on gengzi they set out from Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 繹又遣竟陵太守王僧辯將舟師萬人，出自漢川，載糧東下。

translations.literal: Yi also sent Jingling prefect Wang Senbian leading ten thousand river troops from Hanchuan, carrying grain eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also sent Jingling prefect Wang Senbian with ten thousand river troops from Hanchuan, carrying grain eastward.

sentences.zh: 方等有俊才，善騎射，每戰，親犯矢石，以死節自任。

translations.literal: Fangdeng had outstanding talent, skilled in riding and archery; in every battle he personally braved arrows and stones, taking death for honor as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdeng was gifted and skilled in riding and archery; in every battle he personally braved arrows and stones, holding death for honor as his charge.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，侯景以火車焚台城東南樓。

translations.literal: On renyin, Hou Jing used fire carts to burn the southeast tower of the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Hou Jing used fire carts to burn the southeast tower of the palace city.

sentences.zh: 材官吳景有巧思，於城內構地為樓，火才滅，新樓即立，賊以為神。

translations.literal: Artificer Wu Jing had clever ingenuity; within the city he built towers from the ground—as soon as fire died, new towers stood; the rebels thought it divine.
translations.idiomatic: Artificer Wu Jing was ingenious; within the city he built towers from the ground—as soon as fire died, new towers stood; the rebels thought it divine.

sentences.zh: 景因火起，潛遣人於其下穿城。

translations.literal: Jing took advantage of the fire to secretly send men to tunnel under the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Jing took advantage of the fire to secretly send men to tunnel under the wall.

sentences.zh: 城將崩，乃覺之；

translations.literal: The wall was about to collapse before they noticed;
translations.idiomatic: The wall was about to collapse before they noticed;

sentences.zh: 吳景於城內更築迂城，狀如卻月以擬之，兼擲火，焚其攻具，賊乃退走。

translations.literal: Wu Jing within the city built a curved inner wall shaped like a crescent moon to counter it, and also threw fire, burning their siege engines; the rebels then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing built a curved inner wall shaped like a crescent moon to counter it, and threw fire, burning their siege engines; the rebels retreated.

sentences.zh: 太子遣洗馬元孟恭將千人自大司馬門出蕩，孟恭與左右奔降於景。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince sent Groom of the Heir Yuan Menggong leading a thousand men out from the Grand Marshal Gate to clear the area; Menggong and his attendants fled and surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent groom of the heir Yuan Menggong with a thousand men out from the Grand Marshal Gate to clear the area; Menggong and his attendants fled and surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 己酉，景土山稍逼城樓，柳津命作地道以取其土，外山崩，壓賊且盡。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Jing's earthen mounds gradually pressed close to the tower; Liu Jin ordered tunnels dug to take their earth; the outer mound collapsed and crushed nearly all the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Jing's earthen mounds gradually pressed close to the tower; Liu Jin ordered tunnels dug to remove their earth; the outer mound collapsed and crushed nearly all the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又於城內作飛橋，懸罩二土山上。

translations.literal: Within the city they also built flying bridges, suspended to cover the two earthen mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city they also built flying bridges, suspended to cover the two earthen mounds.

sentences.zh: 景眾見飛橋迥出，崩騰而走；

translations.literal: Jing's troops saw the flying bridges jutting out and fled in panicked collapse;
translations.idiomatic: Jing's troops saw the flying bridges jutting out and fled in panic;

sentences.zh: 城內擲雉尾炬，焚其東山，樓柵蕩盡，賊積死於城下，乃棄土山不復修，自焚其攻具。

translations.literal: within the city they threw pheasant-tail torches, burned their eastern mound, towers and palisades were swept away, rebels piled dead below the wall—they then abandoned the earthen mounds and did not rebuild, burning their own siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: within the city they threw pheasant-tail torches, burned the eastern mound, towers and palisades were swept away, rebels piled dead below the wall—they abandoned the earthen mounds, burned their siege engines, and did not rebuild.

sentences.zh: 材官將軍宋嶷降於景，教之引玄武湖水以灌台城，闕前皆為洪流。

translations.literal: Artificer General Song Ni surrendered to Jing and taught him to draw Xuanwu Lake water to flood the palace city; before the gate all became a torrent.
translations.idiomatic: Artificer general Song Ni surrendered to Jing and taught him to draw Xuanwu Lake water to flood the palace city; before the gate all became a torrent.

sentences.zh: 上征衡州刺史韋粲為散騎常侍，以都督長沙歐陽頠監州事。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Hengzhou Inspector Wei Can as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant and had Changsha Supervisor Ouyang Gu oversee provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Hengzhou inspector Wei Can as supernumerary cavalier attendant and had Changsha supervisor Ouyang Gu oversee provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 粲，放之子也。

translations.literal: Can was Fang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Can was the son of Wei Fang.

sentences.zh: 還，至廬陵，聞侯景亂，粲簡閱部下，得精兵五千，倍道赴援。

translations.literal: Returning, he reached Luling; hearing of Hou Jing's rebellion, Can inspected his subordinates, got five thousand elite troops, and raced by double stages to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he reached Luling; hearing of Hou Jing's rebellion, Can inspected his subordinates, mustered five thousand elite troops, and raced to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 至豫章，聞景已出橫江，粲就內史劉孝儀謀之，孝儀曰：「必如此，當有敕。

translations.literal: Reaching Yuzhang, he heard Jing had already crossed Hengjiang; Can consulted with Administrator Liu Xiaoyi, who said, "If it were truly so, there would be an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yuzhang, he heard Jing had already crossed Hengjiang; Can consulted with administrator Liu Xiaoyi, who said, "If it were truly so, there would be an edict.

sentences.zh: 豈可輕信人言，妄相驚動！

translations.literal: How can one lightly trust men's words and recklessly stir alarm!
translations.idiomatic: How can one lightly trust rumor and recklessly stir alarm!

sentences.zh: 或恐不然。

translations.literal: Perhaps it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps it is not so.

sentences.zh: 」時孝儀置酒，粲怒，以杯抵地曰：「賊已渡江，便逼宮闕，水陸俱斷，何暇有報！

translations.literal: " At the time Xiaoyi was setting out wine; Can angrily dashed his cup to the ground and said, "The rebels have crossed the river and now press the palace—land and water routes are both cut; how is there time for reports!
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Xiaoyi was setting out wine; Can angrily dashed his cup to the ground: "The rebels have crossed the river and now press the palace—land and water routes are both cut; how is there time for reports!

sentences.zh: 假令無敕，豈得自安！

translations.literal: Even if there were no edict, how could one rest at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Even if there were no edict, how could one rest at ease!

sentences.zh: 韋粲今日何情飲酒！

translations.literal: What mood has Wei Can today to drink wine!
translations.idiomatic: What mood has Wei Can today to drink wine!

sentences.zh: 」即馳馬出部分。

translations.literal: " He immediately galloped out to deploy his forces.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately galloped out to deploy his forces.

sentences.zh: 將發，會江州刺史當陽公大心遣使邀粲，粲乃馳往見大心曰：「上游籓鎮，江州去京最近，殿下情計誠宜在前。

translations.literal: About to set out, he met an envoy from Jiangzhou Inspector Prince of Dangyang Daxin inviting Can; Can galloped to see Daxin and said, "Among upstream frontier posts, Jiangzhou is nearest the capital—Your Highness by feeling and plan should truly take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: About to set out, he met an envoy from Jiangzhou inspector Prince Daxin of Dangyang inviting him; Can galloped to see Daxin and said, "Among upstream frontier posts, Jiangzhou is nearest the capital—Your Highness should truly take the lead.

sentences.zh: 但中流任重，當須應接，不可闕鎮。

translations.literal: But the midstream burden is heavy—you must receive and respond; the post cannot be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: But the midstream burden is heavy—you must hold the line; the post cannot be left vacant.

sentences.zh: 今宜且張聲勢，移鎮湓城，遣偏將賜隨，於事便足。

translations.literal: Now you should first raise a show of force, move your seat to Pencheng, and send a subordinate general to follow— that will suffice for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should raise a show of force, move your seat to Pencheng, and send a subordinate general to follow—that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」大心然之，遣中兵柳昕帥兵二千人隨粲，粲至南洲，外弟司州刺史柳仲禮亦帥步騎萬餘人至橫江，粲即送糧仗贍給之，並散私金帛以賞其戰士。

translations.literal: " Daxin agreed, sent Central Troops Commander Liu Xin leading two thousand men to follow Can; Can reached Nanzhou; his cousin by marriage, Sizhou Inspector Liu Zhongli, also led more than ten thousand foot and horse to Hengjiang; Can immediately sent grain and arms to supply him and distributed private gold and silk to reward his warriors.
translations.idiomatic: " Daxin agreed and sent central troops commander Liu Xin with two thousand men to follow Can. Can reached Nanzhou; his cousin by marriage, Sizhou inspector Liu Zhongli, also led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to Hengjiang. Can immediately sent grain and arms to supply him and distributed private gold and silk to reward his warriors.

sentences.zh: 西豫州刺史裴之高自張公洲遣船度仲禮，丙辰夜，粲、仲禮及宣猛將軍李孝欽、前司州刺史羊鴉仁、南陵太守陳文徹，合軍屯新林王游苑。

translations.literal: Western Yuzhou Inspector Pei Zhigao sent boats from Zhanggong Isle to ferry Zhongli; on the night of bingchen, Can, Zhongli, Xuanmeng General Li Xiaoqin, former Sizhou Inspector Yang Yaren, and Nanling prefect Chen Wenche combined armies and encamped at the Princes' Pleasure Garden of Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yuzhou inspector Pei Zhigao sent boats from Zhanggong Isle to ferry Zhongli. On the night of bingchen, Can, Zhongli, Xuanmeng general Li Xiaoqin, former Sizhou inspector Yang Yaren, and Nanling prefect Chen Wenche combined armies and encamped at the Princes' Pleasure Garden of Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 粲議推仲禮為大都督，報下流眾軍；

translations.literal: Can proposed making Zhongli supreme commander and reporting this to downstream armies;
translations.idiomatic: Can proposed making Zhongli supreme commander and reporting this to downstream armies;

sentences.zh: 裴之高自以年位，恥居其下，議累日不決。

translations.literal: Pei Zhigao, considering his age and rank, was ashamed to serve under him; deliberation went unresolved for days.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigao, considering his age and rank, was ashamed to serve under him; deliberation went unresolved for days.

sentences.zh: 粲抗言於眾曰：「今者同赴國難，義在除賊。

translations.literal: Can spoke forcefully before the assembly: "Today we alike go to the state's peril—the righteous task is to destroy the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Can spoke forcefully before the assembly: "Today we alike go to the state's peril—the righteous task is to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 所以推柳司州者，正以久捍邊疆，先為侯景所憚；

translations.literal: The reason for proposing Sizhou Inspector Liu is precisely that he long defended the frontier and is already feared by Hou Jing;
translations.idiomatic: The reason for proposing Sizhou inspector Liu is precisely that he long defended the frontier and is already feared by Hou Jing;

sentences.zh: 且士馬精銳，無出其前。

translations.literal: moreover his men and horses are keen—none surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: moreover his men and horses are keen—none surpass him.

sentences.zh: 若論位次，柳在粲下，語其年齒，亦少於粲，直以社稷之計，不得復論。

translations.literal: If one speaks of rank, Liu is below Can; speaking of age, he is also younger than Can—only for the state's sake can we speak no further of this.
translations.idiomatic: By rank Liu is below Can; by age he is younger—only for the state's sake can we speak no further of this.

sentences.zh: 今日形勢，貴在將和，若人心不同，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Today's situation values generals in harmony; if hearts differ, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation values unity among commanders; if hearts differ, the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 裴公朝之舊德，豈應復挾私情以沮大計！

translations.literal: Lord Pei is an old pillar of the court—how should he again let private feeling obstruct the great plan!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pei is an old pillar of the court—how can he let private feeling obstruct the great plan!

sentences.zh: 粲請為諸軍解之。

translations.literal: Can asks to settle this for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Let Can settle this for the armies.

sentences.zh: 」乃單舸至之高營，切讓之曰：「今二宮危逼，猾寇滔天，臣子當戮力同心，豈可自相矛盾！

translations.literal: " He then went alone in a single boat to Zhigao's camp and sharply reproached him: "Now the two palaces are in dire peril, the cunning rebels fill the sky—ministers and sons should join strength in one heart; how can we oppose each other!
translations.idiomatic: " He then went alone in a single boat to Zhigao's camp and sharply reproached him: "Now the two palaces are in dire peril, cunning rebels fill the sky—ministers and sons should join in one heart; how can we oppose each other!

sentences.zh: 豫州必欲立異，鋒鏑便有所歸。

translations.literal: If Yuzhou insists on standing apart, blades and arrows will know where to go.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuzhou insists on standing apart, blades and arrows will know where to go.

sentences.zh: 」之高垂泣致謝。

translations.literal: " Zhigao wept and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhigao wept and apologized.

sentences.zh: 遂推仲禮為大都督。

translations.literal: They then made Zhongli supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: They then made Zhongli supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 宣城內史楊白華遣其子雄將郡兵繼至，援軍大集，眾十餘萬，緣淮樹柵，景亦於北岸樹柵以應之。

translations.literal: Xuancheng Administrator Yang Baihua sent his son Xiong leading district troops to follow; relief armies greatly gathered—more than a hundred thousand—building palisades along the Huai; Jing also built palisades on the north bank to match.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng administrator Yang Baihua sent his son Xiong with district troops; relief armies gathered in force—more than a hundred thousand—building palisades along the Huai; Jing also built palisades on the north bank to match.

sentences.zh: 裴之高與弟之橫以舟師一萬屯張公洲。

translations.literal: Pei Zhigao and his brother Zhihéng encamped at Zhanggong Isle with ten thousand river troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigao and his brother Zhihéng encamped at Zhanggong Isle with ten thousand river troops.

sentences.zh: 景囚之高弟、侄、子、孫、臨水陳兵，連鎖列於陳前，以鼎鑊、刀鋸隨其後，謂曰：「裴公不降，今即烹之。

translations.literal: Jing imprisoned Zhigao's younger brothers, nephews, sons, and grandsons; facing the water he arrayed troops, chains lined before the battle line, cauldrons and knives and saws behind, and said, "If Lord Pei does not surrender, they will be boiled now.
translations.idiomatic: Jing imprisoned Zhigao's younger brothers, nephews, sons, and grandsons; facing the water he arrayed troops, chains lined before the battle line, cauldrons and knives and saws behind, and said, "If Lord Pei does not surrender, they will be boiled now.

sentences.zh: 」之高召善射者使射其子，再發，皆不中。

translations.literal: " Zhigao summoned skilled archers to shoot at his son; twice they loosed, both missed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhigao summoned skilled archers to shoot at his son; twice they loosed, both missed.

sentences.zh: 景帥步騎萬人於後渚挑戰，仲禮欲出擊之。

translations.literal: Jing led ten thousand foot and horse to challenge at Rear Islet; Zhongli wished to sally and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to challenge at Rear Islet; Zhongli wished to sally and strike.

sentences.zh: 韋粲曰：「日晚我勞，未可戰也。

translations.literal: Wei Can said, "It is late and we are weary—not yet time to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Can said, "It is late and we are weary—not yet time to fight.

sentences.zh: 」仲禮乃堅壁不出，景亦引退。

translations.literal: " Zhongli then held the walls and did not come out; Jing also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongli then held the walls and did not come out; Jing also withdrew.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹將銳卒三萬發江陵，留其子綏寧侯方諸居守，咨議參軍劉之迡等三上箋請留，答教不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi was about to lead thirty thousand crack troops from Jiangling, leaving his son Marquis of Suining Fangzhu to hold the seat; Advisory Staff Officer Liu Zhituo and others thrice submitted memorials asking him to stay—the written reply did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong was about to lead thirty thousand crack troops from Jiangling, leaving his son Marquis Fangzhu of Suining to hold the seat; advisory staff officer Liu Zhituo and others thrice submitted memorials asking him to stay—the written reply refused.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王范遣其將梅伯龍攻王顯貴於壽陽，克其羅城；

translations.literal: Prince of Poyang Fan sent his general Mei Bolong to attack Wang Xiangui at Shouchun and took the outer wall;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Fan of Poyang sent his general Mei Bolong to attack Wang Xiangui at Shouchun and took the outer wall;

sentences.zh: 攻中城，不克而退，范益其眾，使復攻之。

translations.literal: attacking the inner city, he could not take it and withdrew; Fan increased his forces and had him attack again.
translations.idiomatic: attacking the inner city, he could not take it and withdrew; Fan increased his forces and had him attack again.

sentences.zh: 東魏大將軍澄患民錢濫惡，議不禁民私鑄，但懸稱市門，錢不重五銖，毋得入市。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand General Cheng was troubled that people's coin was debased and poor; he proposed not forbidding private minting but posting scales at market gates—coin not weighing five zhu was not to enter the market.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei grand general Gao Cheng was troubled that people's coin was debased; he proposed not forbidding private minting but posting scales at market gates—coin not weighing five zhu was not to enter the market.

sentences.zh: 朝議以為年谷不登，請俟它年，乃止。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that the year's grain had not ripened and asked to wait for another year—it was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation held that the year's harvest had failed and asked to wait for another year—the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 魏太師泰殺安定國臣王茂而非其罪。

translations.literal: Wei Grand Preceptor Tai killed Wang Mao, minister of Anding, though he was not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei grand preceptor Yuwen Tai killed Wang Mao, minister of Anding, though he was not guilty.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞柳慶諫，泰怒曰：「卿黨罪人，亦當坐！

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Liu Qing remonstrated; Tai angrily said, "You shield the guilty—you too should be punished!
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant director of the secretariat Liu Qing remonstrated; Yuwen Tai angrily said, "You shield the guilty—you too should be punished!

sentences.zh: 」執慶於前。

translations.literal: " He seized Qing before him.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized Qing before him.

sentences.zh: 慶辭色不撓，曰：「慶聞君蔽於事為不明，臣知而不爭為不忠。

translations.literal: Qing's words and bearing did not bend; he said, "Qing has heard that a lord blinded to affairs is unwise, and a minister who knows yet does not contend is disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's words and bearing did not bend; he said, "I have heard that a lord blinded to affairs is unwise, and a minister who knows yet does not contend is disloyal.

sentences.zh: 慶既竭忠，不敢愛死，但懼公為不明耳。

translations.literal: Qing having exhausted loyalty, dares not cherish life—only fears that my lord is unwise.
translations.idiomatic: Having exhausted my loyalty, I dare not cherish life—only fear that my lord is unwise.

sentences.zh: 」泰寤，亟使赦茂，不及，乃賜茂家錢帛，曰：「以旌吾過。

translations.literal: " Tai awoke and urgently sent to pardon Mao—too late; he then bestowed money and silk on Mao's family, saying, "To mark my fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai awoke and urgently sent to pardon Mao—too late; he then bestowed money and silk on Mao's family, saying, "To mark my fault.

sentences.zh: 丙辰晦，柳仲禮夜入韋粲營，部分眾軍。

translations.literal: On the last day of bingchen, Liu Zhongli entered Wei Can's camp by night and deployed the armies.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of bingchen, Liu Zhongli entered Wei Can's camp by night and deployed the armies.

sentences.zh: 旦日，會戰，諸將各有據守，令粲頓青塘。

translations.literal: At dawn, they joined battle; each general had his post; Can was ordered to hold Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they joined battle; each general had his post; Can was ordered to hold Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 粲以青塘當石頭中路，賊必爭之，頗憚之。

translations.literal: Can, because Qingtang lay on the central road to Shitou and the rebels would surely contest it, was quite afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Can, because Qingtang lay on the central road to Shitou and the rebels would surely contest it, was quite afraid.

sentences.zh: 仲禮曰：「青塘要地，非兄不可；

translations.literal: Zhongli said, "Qingtang is a vital ground—no one but elder brother will do;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli said, "Qingtang is vital ground—no one but you will do;

sentences.zh: 若疑兵少，當更遣軍相助。

translations.literal: if you fear too few troops, more should be sent to assist.
translations.idiomatic: if you fear too few troops, more will be sent to assist.

sentences.zh: 」乃使直閣將軍劉叔胤助之。

translations.literal: " He then sent Direct Attendant General Liu Shuyin to assist.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent direct attendant general Liu Shuyin to assist.
